_comment: Conformance vectors for the hub attention engine (spec/household_keys_v0.md section 7; the `attention` and `household_posture` blocks of spec/witness_dictionary.json).
HAND-AUTHORED. Every expectation was decided from the dictionary's rules, not computed by an engine; never regenerate this file from code. Change the dictionary first, then this file, then the code.

vectors: {name, input, expect}. Every input spells all eleven fields; `corroboration` is the list of channel ids that agreed (the reporting channel's own included), and a replay counts the DISTINCT modality classes among them (wifi_rf and ble are one class; unknown counts for nothing). `expect` is the whole decision: tier, phrase, reason, held_for_morning (quiet hours holding a digest) and the episode key {family, zone}.
words: each device_word (exact, case-sensitive; anything unlisted is `other`) or kernel_event_type (the kernel's PascalCase wire form) and its class.

episodes: timed sequences for the repeat governor, on monotonic seconds. Each step is {at, tier, episode, expect}; expect is notify {cause}, collapsed {resting_for_secs} or not_surfaced. The numbers are the Apple apps' RepeatGovernor: 120 s doubling to 1800 s, an 1800 s calm gap measured from the latest second any repeat was considered (a stamp earlier than that is recorded as that latest second, so a stray early one can neither fake a calm nor shorten a rest), a higher tier always notifies, critical is never governed; tier none is never considered.

Replayed by: src/relay/attention.rs (Rust, run by rust.yml's `cargo test --features alert-relay relay::`). Any other surface that decides tiers (the Apple apps, the display, the Home Assistant integration) must replay this file before it ships its own copy of the rules.
